title: I created Foilsmith: a free tool that makes holographic trading cards from any art
author: Jag783
selftext:
I wanted shiny cards for a card game and couldn't find a tool that did the whole job, so I built one.

You give Foilsmith a piece of art. It draws a card frame over it and builds the maps a shader needs. The result is a card that tilts toward your mouse, catches the light in a foil finish, and shows real depth through the art window. Click it and it turns over to the back.

What it does:

- Frames: a frame is a stack of parts: art window, title bars, text boxes, symbols, attacks and stats. There are four presets (classic, duel, pocket, full-art), and you can change any part, the colours and the fonts.
- Depth from the art: a local depth model/compute shader separates the subject from the background. That gives you parallax, relief lighting, a shadow on the card and a rim light. The frame never gets depth, so the art looks like it sits behind a window.
- 10 finishes: standard, holo, cracked ice, gold, galaxy, glitch, arcane, inverse, engraved and spectrum. Each one has sliders.
- Pixel art: detected automatically. It gets nearest-neighbour sampling and stepped foil hues.
- Card backs: the default back or your own image. The back can take the foil too.

Three ways to use it:

1. Web app: https://foilsmith.dev/ Upload art, build the frame and see the card live in WebGL. Everything runs in your browser through WebAssembly
2. Godot 4.4+ addon: a FoilsmithCard node. You build the frame in the scene tree and bake depth on the GPU in the editor. The card is saved as plain PNGs and a JSON file, so your game just loads images. Free on itch.io: https://neotryptophan.itch.io/foilsmith. If it's useful to you, you can pay what you want when you download it. Donations help me keep working on Foilsmith.
3. CLI: foilsmith card.json -o out/ --preview card.gif writes the maps, the layers and an animated GIF, WebP, WebM or MP4 preview. It also handles a whole folder of cards in one go.

Card files and frame templates work in all three tools, so something you design in the browser opens in Godot.

It's written in Rust and MIT licensed. The shaders for Godot and WebGL/GLSL are in the repo if you'd rather use your own engine: https://github.com/Tryptophan/foilsmith
